transcript.text: Every time I put the oven on it runs for a few minutes and then the trip switch goes and half the house loses power. Reset it 3 times tonight. Hotpoint built-in, about 9 years old. What could cause this?

This is a serious safety issue that requires immediate attention. Please stop using the oven until it has been inspected by a qualified electrician.

The fact that resetting the trip switch (likely an RCD or RCBO) multiple times in one evening indicates a persistent and potentially dangerous fault. Here’s what could be causing this:

### Most Likely Causes

1.  Earth Fault (Leakage to Earth)
• This is the most common reason for an RCD/RCBO trip when using high-power appliances like ovens.
• Something inside the oven (heating element, wiring, motor, or control board) has developed a fault where electricity is leaking to the metal casing or earth wire.
• The RCD detects this imbalance and trips to prevent electric shock.

2.  Overloaded Circuit
• If the oven shares a circuit with other high-draw appliances (e.g., another oven, induction hob, electric shower, or multiple heaters), turning on the oven may exceed the circuit’s capacity.
• However, if it trips every time you turn it on—even when no other devices are running—it’s less likely to be pure overload and more likely a fault.

3.  Faulty Heating Element
• The main bake or grill element may have cracked internally, allowing current to leak to earth. This is common in older ovens (9 years is within the range for such failures).

4.  Wiring Issue Inside the Oven
• Loose connections, damaged insulation, or a short circuit within the oven’s internal wiring can cause intermittent faults that trigger the trip switch.

5.  Faulty RCD/RCBO Itself
• Less commonly, the trip switch itself may be faulty or overly sensitive. However, since it happens specifically when the oven is on, the oven is the probable culprit.

6.  Moisture or Condensation
• If there’s been recent cleaning with water near electrical components, or if steam has entered the control panel, it could cause a temporary earth fault.

### Why It’s Dangerous to Keep Resetting

• Fire Risk: An earth fault can generate heat and potentially lead to an electrical fire.
• Electric Shock Hazard: If the oven casing becomes live due to an earth fault, anyone touching it could receive a shock.
• Damage to Appliances: Repeated tripping can damage other electronics on the same circuit.

### What You Should Do Immediately

1.  Stop Using the Oven: Do not attempt to use it again until it’s been checked.
2.  Call a Qualified Electrician: This is not a DIY fix. An electrician will:
• Isolate the oven from the circuit.
• Test for earth faults using insulation resistance testing equipment.
• Check the heating elements and internal wiring.
• Determine if the oven needs repair or replacement.
3.  Consider Age: At 9 years old, your Hotpoint oven is nearing the end of its typical lifespan (often 10–15 years). If the repair cost is high, it may be more economical to replace the unit entirely.

### Temporary Workaround (Not a Solution)

• You could try plugging the oven into a different circuit if your home has multiple radial circuits for kitchen appliances—but only if you are confident in doing so safely and only as a diagnostic step. If it trips on another circuit, the fault is definitely in the oven. If it doesn’t trip, the issue may be with the original circuit or overload. However, this should still be done by an electrician to avoid risk.

Please prioritize safety: contact a professional electrician today.
